interventions.name: Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES)
interventions.source_text: Advise all people with diabetes to participate in developmentally and culturally appropriate diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) to facilitate informed decision-making, self-care behaviors, problem-solving, and active collaboration with the health care team.

interventions.name: Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT)
interventions.source_text: All people with diabetes should be referred for individualized MNT provided by an RDN who is experienced and skilled in providing diabetes-specific MNT (76–78), at diagnosis and as needed throughout the life span, like DSMES.

interventions.name: Behavioral strategies
interventions.source_text: Use behavioral strategies (e.g., motivational interviewing, goal setting, problem-solving) to support DSMES and engagement in behaviors known to optimize health-related quality of life and outcomes.

interventions.name: Telehealth DSMES
interventions.source_text: Offer DSMES via telehealth and/or digital interventions to meet individual preferences, reduce access barriers, and improve satisfaction.

interventions.name: Metabolic Surgery
interventions.source_text: Engagement in exercise programs prior to and after metabolic surgery may support muscle mass and strength (315,316), reduce weight recurrence and promote better weight maintenance (317,318), and improve insulin sensitivity (319).

interventions.name: Obesity pharmacotherapy
interventions.source_text: In addition to metabolic surgery, combining obesity pharmacotherapy with exercise programs may lead to some synergistic benefits.

interventions.name: Combination treatment for smoking cessation
interventions.source_text: For individuals who use these products, provide or refer for combination treatment consisting of tobacco and/or vape product(s) cessation counseling and pharmacologic therapy.

interventions.name: Psychosocial care
interventions.source_text: Provide psychosocial care to all people with diabetes as part of routine medical care delivered by trained health care professionals using a collaborative, person-centered, culturally informed approach.

interventions.name: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)
interventions.source_text: Successful evidence-based approaches include cognitive behavioral (392,396,412) and mindfulness-based therapies (413).

interventions.name: Mindfulness-based therapies
interventions.source_text: Successful evidence-based approaches include cognitive behavioral (392,396,412) and mindfulness-based therapies (413).

interventions.name: Collaborative care
interventions.source_text: Person-centered integrated care approaches have been shown to improve both depression and glycemic outcomes (5).

interventions.name: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP)
interventions.source_text: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) significantly reduced A1C by 0.24% (561).

behaviors.name: Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES) participation
behaviors.source_text: Advise all people with diabetes to participate in developmentally and culturally appropriate diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) to facilitate informed decision-making, self-care behaviors, problem-solving, and active collaboration with the health care team.
behaviors.target_amount: At diagnosis, annually and/or when not meeting treatment goals, when complicating factors develop, and when transitions in life and care occur.

behaviors.name: Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT) engagement
behaviors.source_text: All people with diabetes should be referred for individualized MNT provided by an RDN who is experienced and skilled in providing diabetes-specific MNT (76–78), at diagnosis and as needed throughout the life span, like DSMES.

behaviors.name: Mediterranean eating pattern
behaviors.source_text: Counsel people with diabetes and those at risk for diabetes to consider an eating plan emphasizing elements of a Mediterranean eating pattern, which is rich in fatty fish, nuts, and seeds, to reduce cardiovascular disease risk A and improve glucose metabolism. B

behaviors.name: Cessation of tobacco products and vaping
behaviors.source_text: support for cessation of tobacco products and vaping

behaviors.name: 150 min/week moderate- to vigorous-intensity aerobic activity
behaviors.source_text: Counsel most adults with type 1 diabetes C and type 2 diabetes B to engage in 150 min or more of moderate- to vigorous-intensity aerobic activity per week, spread over at least 3 days/week, with no more than 2 consecutive days without activity.

behaviors.name: Resistance exercise
behaviors.source_text: Counsel most adults with type 1 diabetes C and type 2 diabetes B to engage in 2–3 sessions/week of resistance ex- ercise on nonconsecutive days.

behaviors.name: Flexibility and balance training
behaviors.source_text: Most older adults with diabetes are encouraged to participate in flexibility and balance training 2–3 times/week.

behaviors.name: Smoking cessation
behaviors.source_text: Ask people with diabetes routinely about the use of tobacco or vape products. A Advise complete avoidance of tobacco and vaping. A

behaviors.name: Limiting sodium consumption
behaviors.source_text: Counsel people with diabetes to limit sodium consumption to <2,300 mg/day, as clinically appropriate, and the best way to achieve this is through limiting consumption of processed foods. B

behaviors.name: Consuming water
behaviors.source_text: Encourage people with diabetes and those at risk for diabetes to consume water over other beverages. A

behaviors.name: Minimizing refined carbohydrates
behaviors.source_text: minimize consumption of red meat, sugar-sweetened beverages, sweets, refined grains, processed and ultraprocessed foods in people with prediabetes and diabetes. B

behaviors.name: Weight loss of at least 5-7%
behaviors.source_text: Provide an overweight or obesity treatment plan based on their nutrition, physical activity, and behavioral health status for all people with overweight or obesity, aiming for at least 5–7% weight loss. A

behaviors.name: Breaking up prolonged sitting
behaviors.source_text: Breaking up prolonged sitting (at least every 30 min) with short regular bouts of slow walking or simple resistance exercises can improve glucose metabolism.

behaviors.name: Consistent sleep schedule
behaviors.source_text: Aim for consistent, uninterrupted sleep, even on weekends.

social_determinants.name: Food insecurity
social_determinants.source_text: In 2023, 13.5% of Americans were food insecure (238), and food insecurity affects 16% of adults with diabetes compared with 9% of adults without diabetes (239).

social_determinants.name: Access barriers to DSMES
social_determinants.source_text: Identify and address barriers to DSMES that exist at the payor, health system, clinic, health care professional, and individual levels.

social_determinants.name: Technology access
social_determinants.source_text: The DSMES team needs to consider characteristics such as racial identity, ethnic and cultural background, biological sex and gender identity, age, geographic location, technology access, education, literacy, and numeracy (13).

social_determinants.name: Financial barriers
social_determinants.source_text: These nontraditional versions of DSMES may not always be reimbursed; however, adopting reimbursement policies that increase DSMES access and use will positively affect beneficiaries’ clinical outcomes, quality of life, health care use, and costs (10,58).

outcomes.name: Improved glycemic outcomes
outcomes.source_text: DSMES can improve outcomes and reduce costs, so reimbursement by third-party payors is recommended. B

outcomes.name: Weight loss
outcomes.source_text: An example of this is from an RCT that tested DSMES in a virtual environment that demonstrated greater weight loss and similar decreases in A1C, blood pressure, cholesterol, and triglycerides compared with DSMES via a standard website (57).

outcomes.name: Reduced A1C
outcomes.source_text: found to produce a greater reduction in A1C (−0.30 percentage points; 95% CI −0.42 to −0.19) compared with control (42).

outcomes.name: Improved cardiometabolic outcomes
outcomes.source_text: Diabetes medical nutrition therapy can result in cost savings B and improved cardiometabolic outcomes A and should be reimbursed by insurance. E

outcomes.source_text: Counsel people with diabetes and those at risk for diabetes to consider an eating plan emphasizing elements of a Mediterranean eating pattern, which is rich in fatty fish, nuts, and seeds, to reduce cardiovascular disease risk A and improve glucose metabolism. B

outcomes.name: Improved glucose metabolism
outcomes.source_text: Counsel people with diabetes and those at risk for diabetes to consider an eating plan emphasizing elements of a Mediterranean eating pattern, which is rich in fatty fish, nuts, and seeds, to reduce cardiovascular disease risk A and improve glucose metabolism. B

outcomes.name: Reduced risk of hypoglycemia
outcomes.source_text: Counsel people using fixed insulin doses about consistent patterns of carbohydrate intake with respect to time and amount while considering the insulin action time, as it can result in improved glycemia and reduce the risk for hypoglycemia. B

outcomes.name: Improved quality of life
outcomes.source_text: The overall objectives of DSMES are to support informed decision-making, self-care behaviors, problem-solving, and active collaboration with the health care team to improve clinical outcomes, health status, and well-being in a cost-effective manner (2).

outcomes.name: Reduced diabetes distress
outcomes.source_text: An RCT of CBT in adults with type 2 diabetes showed a reduction in health anxiety, with CBT accounting for 77% of the reduction in health anxiety at 16 weeks of follow-up; this trial also found decreased depressive symptoms and diabetes distress (461).

outcomes.name: Reduced depressive symptoms
outcomes.source_text: An RCT of CBT in adults with type 2 diabetes showed a reduction in health anxiety, with CBT accounting for 77% of the reduction in health anxiety at 16 weeks of follow-up; this trial also found decreased depressive symptoms and diabetes distress (461).

outcomes.name: Reduced risk of CVD
outcomes.source_text: A systematic review and meta-analysis comparing those who quit smoking to those who smoke stratified by postcessation weight gain found smoking cessation lowered the risk of CVD and all-cause mortality regardless of postcessation weight gain (345).

outcomes.source_text: A systematic review and meta-analysis comparing those who quit smoking to those who smoke stratified by postcessation weight gain found smoking cessation lowered the risk of CVD and all-cause mortality regardless of postcessation weight gain (345).
